extracted.intended_audience: investigative journalists, accountability reporters, and newsletter editors
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria for selecting and vetting accountability-focused stories (especially for newsletters) that expose corporate or political inconsistency and create pressure on the powerful. Emphasizes document-based reporting, patterns over isolated incidents, and practical tests for publishability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hidden corporate-political linkages
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify donations, lobbying, board seats, or other connections that are inconsistent with an entity's public branding or stated positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for documentary evidence (donor lists, lobbying filings, board rosters) showing relationships that the company/brand does not advertise; emphasize ties that reveal hypocrisy or influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hypocrisy receipts
rubrics_metrics.description: Show cases where a company or official publicly says X but funds or supports Y that contradicts that position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document both the public claim(s) and financial/organizational behavior that contradicts them; use receipts (payments, contributions, memberships) to prove inconsistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voter suppression actions (by officials and corporate enablers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Expose actions that suppress voting and highlight corporate or private actors who enable or fund them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trace funding, legal support, or logistical assistance from corporations or PACs to voter suppression initiatives; establish links with filings, contracts, statements, or other paper evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti-LGBTQ legislation funders
rubrics_metrics.description: Reveal who is quietly bankrolling anti-LGBTQ legislative efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use campaign finance records, PAC filings, trade association disclosures, and foundation/grant records to identify funders that are not publicly associated with the legislation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disinformation finance
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify who pays influencers, media, or networks that spread disinformation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow money through ad buys, PR contracts, affiliate payments, and platform disclosures to show financial support for disinformation ecosystems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Worker-treatment vs. PR
rubrics_metrics.description: Contrast public-facing PR claims about workplace culture with actual worker treatment and conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine employee testimony with internal docs, inspection reports, lawsuits, and regulatory records to show a mismatch between messaging and reality.

rubrics_metrics.name: DEI promises vs. behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Expose discrepancies between stated diversity/equity/inclusion commitments and concrete corporate behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use hiring data, board composition, vendor relationships, and internal policies vs outcomes to document gaps between promises and practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is there a paper trail?
rubrics_metrics.description: Require documentary evidence (FEC reports, IRS 990, SEC filings, contracts, emails) to substantiate claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize stories with verifiable public records; examples listed include FEC, IRS 990, and SEC filings as primary sources to cite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Can the company / official respond on the record?
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the subject can be contacted and given an opportunity to respond publicly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attempt on-the-record responses; documented refusals or evasions can themselves be part of the story, but an on-record response strengthens fairness and sourcing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does this reveal a pattern, not just an incident?
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer stories that demonstrate recurring behavior or systemic issues rather than isolated events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assemble multiple data points or instances showing consistency over time or across contexts to establish pattern-based accountability claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Will this story create accountability pressure?
rubrics_metrics.description: Select stories likely to prompt behavioral change by exposing powerful actors to reputational, legal, or political consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess potential downstream effects (public outrage, regulatory scrutiny, advertiser pressure) when deciding newsworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Are mainstream outlets ignoring it because it's 'old news' / partisan?
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether lack of mainstream coverage reflects neglect rather than lack of importance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether mainstream silence is due to assumptions about recency or partisanship; older documents can still reveal new patterns or implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quiet PAC donations
rubrics_metrics.description: Look for nonprofit or PAC contributions that are not widely reported but materially influence politics or policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine PAC filings and dark-money pathways to reveal donors that shield their influence through intermediaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade-association memberships
rubrics_metrics.description: Expose influence exerted through trade associations whose members or policies contradict public corporate statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate trade group lobbying positions and member lists to connect companies to positions they don't publicly own.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsidiary brand entanglements
rubrics_metrics.description: Trace relationships between parent companies and subsidiary brands that allow reputational distance while preserving influence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map corporate structures, ownership, and shared contracts to show how problematic behavior can be outsourced to subsidiaries while parent brands claim innocence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local-level officials with national impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Highlight how actions by local officials can have broader national consequences and identify the actors enabling them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow funding, legal assistance, and networks that allow local measures or officials to influence state or national policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-tail consequences of 'old' stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate how previously reported or 'old' events continue to produce effects worth reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document downstream impacts, continuing harm, or accumulative patterns that make older incidents relevant again.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsworthiness = potential to change behavior of the powerful
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit normative metric: a story's value is its capacity to create real-world accountability by exposing inconsistency or influence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this as a touchstone when weighing pitches: give priority to reporting that can alter incentives or prompt corrective action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patient document review over breaking events
rubrics_metrics.description: Favor slow, document-driven reporting (patient review of records) rather than chasing only breaking events or recency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest time in reviewing filings and archival documents; recognize that careful document work often yields accountability stories mainstream outlets miss.
